- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) and forecast remains elevated, lower the forecast by 3–5% to reflect mean reversion.  
- Avoid forecasting a 30-day trend that diverges from recent 7–14 day average; use rolling mean as a sanity check.  
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes (especially >0.7) are common; cap forecast peaks at 1.2x recent 14-day high.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and forecast is consistently above true outcome, apply a 2–3% downward bias to avoid overconfidence.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., drop after 5–7 days), adjust forecast to reflect this by reducing slope after day 5.
